records.summary: When societies crumble, they leave behind remnants of the old world while forcing survivors to forge new ways of life. A well-designed post-apocalyptic setting blends realism with imaginative storytelling, creating a world where scarcity, survival, and adaptation define the experience. 🔻 What Happens When Societies Fall? Societal collapse doesnʼt happen overnight—itʼs a process influenced by political, economic, environmental, and technological factors. Understanding these dynamics helps create believable and immersive settings.

records.proposedName: The Role of Scale: From Small Villages to Galactic Empires
records.summary: Your world can be as small as a single town or as vast as an interstellar empire. The level of detail and complexity should match the scale. 🏡 Small Villages & Towns – Ideal for character-driven stories, local conflicts, and grassroots mysteries. 🏙 Cities & Kingdoms – Introduce political intrigue, large-scale wars, and economic power struggles. 🌍 Continents & Worlds – Suitable for epic adventures, divine interventions, and world-altering events. 🌌 Galactic Empires – Focus on interplanetary diplomacy, mega-corporations, and cosmic-scale threats. 📌 Worldbuilding Tip:Start small, expand organically. Develop one detailed area, then zoom out as needed.

records.summary: A compelling world is more than just geography and magic—it has history, politics, and change. By crafting a dynamic past and evolving systems of power, you create a world that feels alive. This guide covers historical development, political evolution, economic structures, and major societal shifts to help shape immersive settings for TTRPGs and storytelling.

records.summary: Not all settings need encyclopedias of lore. A minimalist approach focuses on core themes and player- driven discovery. ✔ Start with a Strong Premise:“A world where magic is slowly dying” or “A civilization built inside a massive creature.” ✔ Leave Gaps for Discovery: Donʼt define everything—allow room for interpretation and improvisation. ✔ Use Implied Lore: A single strange artifact, inscription, or NPC rumor can suggest a vast unseen history. ✔ Restrict Information: If the players only know what their characters know, mystery becomes a core part of the setting. 📌 Worldbuilding Tip: Challenge yourself to describe an entire setting in one paragraph—what are the most essential details?

records.proposedName: Writing Wars, Revolutions, and Cultural Shifts
records.summary: Wars and revolutions reshape the world, leaving scars for generations. Consider: ✔ Causes of War – Resources, ideology, revenge, power struggles, foreign interference. ✔ Scale of Conflict – Small rebellions, continental wars, interstellar conflicts? ✔ Weapons & Tactics – Medieval sieges, magical warfare, cyber-enhanced soldiers? ✔ Consequences – Borders redrawn, economies collapsed, cultures displaced? ✔ Post-War Rebuilding – How does the world recover? Who gains power? 📌 Worldbuilding Tip: Wars donʼt just end—they create veterans, grudges, and power vacuums that shape future conflicts.

records.summary: “Youʼre not in one world. Youʼre in all of them. Some just havenʼt noticed you yet.” — Traveler Saying

description: “Youʼre not in one world. Youʼre in all of them. Some just havenʼt noticed you yet.” — Traveler Saying
what it means to traverse the multiverse: Operating in the multiverse isnʼt just about hopping from world to world—itʼs about existing in an environment where possibility itself is tangible, layered, and ever-shifting. In Multiversal, adventurers are more than wanderers; they are quantum actors in an interconnected, fluid lattice of timelines, worlds, and branches. Every decision, every movement, and every interaction is potentially reflected in alternate forms across realities— sometimes subtly, sometimes catastrophically. Multiversal dynamics refer to the unique physics, metaphysics, and narrative implications of such a structure. They encompass: •Parallel realities and alternate timelines •Encountering or merging with versions of yourself •Navigating shifting fate currents •Traveling with others while desynced in reality •Moving between branches and resisting multiversal strain Unlike single-world campaigns, multiversal adventures demand a different kind of awareness. Every world has its own "rules," and some rules break when you're not from there. Syncing to a reality can grant power, while resisting its pull may protect your identity—or shred it.
key concepts and foundations: To help players and GMs alike grasp multiversal dynamics, this section will introduce the following foundational ideas: •Reality vs Timeline – A reality is a world with its own laws and traits. A timeline is a linear sequence of events within a reality or set of realities. Timelines can branch, collapse, or merge. •Branch – A large-scale grouping of similar realities, often defined by shared metaphysical laws or origin points. For example, the Mortalitas branch contains death-aligned worlds. •Sync State – A measure of how in-phase a character is with the current reality. Being out-of-sync can cause dissonance, rejection, or even hallucinations. •Echo Selves – Alternate versions of a character that exist in other timelines or realities. Sometimes helpful. Sometimes unhinged. Sometimes already dead. •Fate Currents – Invisible narrative flows that tug at characters, pushing or pulling them toward likely outcomes unless resisted or redirected. •

records.proposedName: Goblin Holes: Pathways of Whispering Chaos
records.summary: Overview: Goblin Holes are a network of tunnels that stretch across the land, burrowing through dimensions and the fabric of reality where chaos has been magically stabilized by goblin sorcerers or engineers. These tunnels, seemingly mundane to the untrained eye, resonate with the latent power of chaos, making them unpredictable and dangerous to all but their goblin creators. The walls of these tunnels are alive with eerie sounds—whispers of the chaos that lies just beyond their bounds, murmuring secrets and temptations to those who dare to travel through them. Discovery and Access: Stumbling upon a Goblin Hole is often accidental, found in the depths of ancient forests, beneath decrepit ruins, or hidden within the dark corners of the world. Accessing these tunnels requires either the guidance of a goblin familiar with their secrets or the acquisition of a key or token, often a magical artifact imbued with the essence of chaos that goblins use to navigate and stabilize the tunnels for safe passage. Traversal Experience: Venturing into a Goblin Hole is not for the faint of heart. The air is thick with a sense of unease, and the walls seem to shift and murmur with voices that are not quite voices, speaking languages that sound almost comprehensible. The path is winding and disorienting, with the sensation that reality itself is thin here, and one wrong step could lead into the maw of chaos. Despite this, for those who know the way, travel through a Goblin Hole can significantly shorten journeys, popping out miles away or even in entirely different realms. Destinations and Consequences: The destinations reached through Goblin Holes can be as unpredictable as the tunnels themselves. While goblins use them to move swiftly between their hidden enclaves or to launch surprise raids, adventurers might find themselves emerging in unexpected locations, from the heart of goblin kingdoms to the edges of reality where the fabric of the world is frayed and strange wonders—or dangers—await.

records.proposedName: Shadow Paths: Veiled Routes of Power and Peril
records.summary: Overview: Shadow Paths are elusive, intangible routes that exist in a state of semi-reality, accessible only under specific conditions or to those with the knowledge or power to unveil them. These paths may weave through the land of shadows, connect darkened doorways across vast distances, or overlay the mortal realm in such a way that travelers can move unseen and undetected by those not attuned to their presence. Discovery and Access: Uncovering a Shadow Path often requires ancient knowledge, a gift bestowed by shadowy entities, or a rare artifact that pierces the veil between light and darkness. Access might be granted only during certain lunar phases, in places where the barrier between worlds is thin, or through rituals that call upon the essence of shadows themselves. The entrance to a Shadow Path might manifest as a darkened alleyway that wasnʼt there before, a mirrorʼs reflection that reveals another world, or a forest shrouded in an unnatural mist. Traversal Experience: Traveling via a Shadow Path is a surreal and disorienting experience, where the familiar rules of time and space may not apply. The path might be shrouded in an impenetrable darkness, illuminated only by strange, phosphorescent flora or the eerie glow of spectral lights. Sounds might be muffled or distorted, and travelers may feel the unnerving sensation of being watched or followed. The journey requires not just physical movement but a mental and spiritual navigation through the darkness. Destinations and Encounters: The destinations reached through Shadow Paths can be as varied as the realms of night themselves, from hidden enclaves of shadow-walkers or secret chambers within ancient ruins, to eerie, parallel versions of the real world where the unseen forces of darkness hold sway. Encounters along these paths might include spirits lost in the shadows, creatures born of darkness, or other travelers who navigate the paths for their own inscrutable purposes.

records.proposedName: The Godmetal Vein That Birthed an Empire
records.summary: “He was a miner. A broken goblin with calloused hands and a voice no one followed. Then the world split open, and every goblin alive heard him scream.” There are no natural portals on Apogine. No gate spells. No stable Translimina veins. The world is sealed—until, one day, it wasnʼt. That breach was not a miracle, but a byproduct of ancient divinity buried in planetary flesh. That breach is known as Garrockʼs Tunnel.

records.summary: “If ruin had a rhythm, Apogine would be its echo. If silence had a shape, it would be built from the bones of this world.” Apogine is not just a planet—it is the final breath of a reality that refused to die. Suspended in the branch of Silentium, Apogine orbits a solitary star beneath a sky devoid of galaxies, moons, or constellations. Its lonely sun gives off a dull and dying light, and the one pale moon that drifts above offers no guidance. It is the last remnant of a universe where everything else has already faded. What defines Apogine is not war, nor magic, nor monsters—but inevitability. Civilizations rise not to flourish, but to collapse with grandeur. Cities are built from the bones of cities built from the bones of cities. Each structure, belief, or power that takes root here is doomed to end, and the residents know this. Whatʼs remarkable is not that things fall apart—but that something always rises again from the rubble, clinging to meaning in the face of total erasure. Apogine is the polar node of the Silentium branch, embodying the full weight of entropy, psychological erosion, and environmental decline. It is one of the most isolated points in the entire multiverse. There are no portals in or out. Even Translimina, the chaotic layer between realities, is shattered and silent beneath its crust. The only known path leads through Garrockʼs Tunnel, a staggering journey of years through the Chaos & Foam. Despite its fatalistic pull, Apogine is not lifeless. Two species dominate its ruins: the Rog, decadent pigfolk clinging to the illusion of empire and opulence; and the Furashin, rodent-like survivors who adapt to every apocalyptic cycle with agility and cunning. Around them swirl echoes of extinct empires, collapsed philosophies, and haunting remnants of technologies that once tried to resist decay.

records.proposedName: This Sunken City Setting in Your Campaign
records.summary: The sunken city offers a versatile setting that can be used for a wide range of adventure types—from treasure hunts and rescue missions to moral dilemmas and supernatural quests. Its blend of underwater mechanics, environmental hazards, ancient magic, and forgotten history provides countless opportunities for creativity, problem-solving, and dynamic storytelling. This environment works especially well for campaigns or one-shots focused on exploration, mystery, and survival. GMs can craft the cityʼs history and culture to connect with other elements in the world, allowing the sunken city to feel like a vital piece of the campaign's puzzle. This Sunken City section equips players and GMs with all the mechanics and tools needed for a memorable and challenging adventure. With environmental hazards, hostile creatures, ancient magic, and intriguing encounters, the ruins promise excitement, danger, and mystery at every turn.

GMs can craft the cityʼs history and culture to connect with other elements in the world, allowing the sunken city to feel like a vital piece of the campaign's puzzle. This Sunken City section equips players and GMs with all the mechanics and tools needed for a memorable and challenging adventure. With environmental hazards, hostile creatures, ancient magic, and intriguing encounters, the ruins promise excitement, danger, and mystery at every turn.

records.summary: Dionasiaʼs past is defined by ambition, catastrophe, and divine intervention. What was once a vibrant, advanced world was undone in a single generation of hubris. The people who survived became stewards of a broken sky, inheritors of fallen greatness. This history is a source of reverence, warning, and unresolved mystery.
